validation.retry_prompt:
Validation failed. Work through these in order; the first two are cheap and catch most failures.

1. IS YOUR BRANCH STALE? .orchestra/validation.sh builds your branch EXACTLY AS IT IS -- it does
   not merge master in first. A fix that is on master is NOT in your build unless it is in your
   branch. Run:
       git fetch upstream && git merge-base --is-ancestor upstream/master HEAD
   If that exits non-zero, rebase onto upstream/master, check that
   'git diff <old-head> <new-head> -- <the files your PR adds or edits>' is EMPTY (this proves
   only the base moved, so any existing approval still stands), force-push, and retry.
   A conflict in FormalSchemes.lean's import list is the usual symptom when a sibling PR landed
   first: take both lines in sorted order and confirm with 'LC_ALL=C sort -c FormalSchemes.lean'.

2. IS IT AN OUT-OF-MEMORY KILL RATHER THAN A PROOF ERROR? 'Lean exited with code 137' with no
   Lean diagnostic is SIGKILL from the OOM killer, not a failed proof. Check whether the failing
   module is one you edited or that imports something you edited. If it is not, the failure is an
   infrastructure problem and not your diff -- say so on the issue and link it rather than
   changing the proof.

3. OTHERWISE, read the log. Re-run 'bash .orchestra/validation.sh' to reproduce, and note that it
   checks four things in order: clean worktree, 'mk_all --check' (every .lean file imported),
   'cache get', then 'lake build --wfail' (warnings are errors).

Do not retry unchanged more than once. A retry that changes nothing about the tree is the same
experiment, and a full validation build costs roughly 25 minutes of shared capacity.
